outline.description: This chapter introduces large-scale language models, the importance of controlling their behavior, and the motivation for aligning them with human preferences.
subtopics: Overview of pre-trained language models (LMs) and their capabilities
Challenges of unsupervised LM training
The concept of model steerability and alignment
Examples of undesired LM behaviors
High-level approaches to alignment
Roadmap of the textbook and key contributions

outline.chapter_title: Human Preference Learning and RLHF Foundations
outline.description: This chapter covers the collection of human preference data, formal models of preference (e.g., Bradley–Terry), and the basics of reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF).
subtopics: Why human preferences? Relative vs. absolute feedback
Data collection: preference comparison tasks
Bradley–Terry and Plackett–Luce preference models
Modeling preferences as binary classification
Introduction to reward functions and latent scoring models
Limitations of pure supervised fine-tuning

outline.description: Here we review key mathematical concepts required for understanding DPO, including maximum likelihood estimation, logistic functions, Kullback–Leibler divergence, and partition functions.
subtopics: Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) refresher
The logistic (sigmoid) function
Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence and its properties
Partition functions and normalization
Policy representations and log‐probabilities
Basics of policy gradient and actor–critic methods

outline.description: This chapter walks through the three phases of traditional RLHF—supervised fine-tuning, reward modeling, and reinforcement learning fine-tuning—highlighting their workflows and challenges.
subtopics: Phase 1: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) of the base LM
Phase 2: Reward modeling with preference data
Formulation of the RLHF objective with KL constraints
Phase 3: Policy optimization using PPO (or REINFORCE)
Practical challenges: instability, sampling overhead, hyperparameter tuning
Case studies in summarization and dialogue

outline.chapter_title: From Reward Modeling to Policy Optimization
outline.description: We explore the relationship between reward models and optimal policies under KL‐constrained objectives, setting the stage for a direct optimization approach.
subtopics: Deriving the optimal policy under a KL‐penalized reward objective
Equation of the form π_r(y|x) ∝ π_ref(y|x)⋅exp(r/β)
Understanding the partition function Z(x)
Reparameterization: expressing rewards in terms of policies
Cancellation of partition functions in preference probabilities
Insight: policy as implicit reward model

outline.chapter_title: Direct Preference Optimization: Derivation and Algorithm
outline.description: This core chapter presents the Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) derivation, loss function, gradient interpretation, and step-by-step algorithmic procedure.
subtopics: Deriving the DPO objective from the Bradley–Terry model
Final DPO loss: binary cross-entropy on log-ratio of policies
Gradient analysis and dynamic importance weights
Algorithm outline and pseudocode for DPO
Implementation details: reference policy initialization, β hyperparameter
Comparison with naïve unlikelihood training

outline.chapter_title: Theoretical Insights and Analysis of DPO
outline.description: We delve into the theoretical underpinnings of DPO, covering reward equivalence classes, identifiability, and connections to actor–critic instabilities.
subtopics: Equivalence classes of reward functions and additive shifts
Lemma: same preference distributions and same optimal policies
Theorem: completeness of the DPO reparameterization
Interpretation within control-as-inference framework
Diagnosing instabilities in actor–critic (PPO) algorithms
Advantages of RL‐free DPO: stability and tractability

outline.description: This chapter reviews experimental results comparing DPO with PPO-based RLHF and other baselines on sentiment control, summarization, and dialogue tasks.
subtopics: Controlled sentiment generation: reward vs. KL frontier
Summarization on Reddit TL;DR: GPT-4 win‐rate evaluation
Single-turn dialogue with Anthropic HH dataset
Evaluation methodologies: GPT-4 prompts and human validation
Best-of-N and Preferred‐FT baselines
Ablations and sensitivity to β and sampling temperature

outline.description: We discuss practical considerations for deploying DPO, best practices, limitations, and potential extensions beyond language models.
subtopics: Selecting and fine‐tuning the reference policy
Reusing public preference datasets
Hyperparameter tuning for β and learning rate
Computational cost comparison with PPO
Scaling DPO to larger models
Extensions to other modalities (vision, audio)
Limitations and open challenges

outline.chapter_title: Future Directions in Preference‐Based Model Training
outline.description: The final chapter outlines open research questions, promising avenues for scaling and improving preference‐driven learning, and broader implications.
subtopics: Generalization under distribution shift
Self-labeling and semi‐supervised preference learning
Reward over‐optimization and campaign risks
Refining automated evaluation with LLMs
Integration with constitutional AI and AI safety frameworks
Applications beyond NLP: robotics, recommendation systems
Ethical considerations and human‐in‐the‐loop design
